# The reasons

The most remarkable chapter of the 1446 book is the one that explains *why*: why
ㄱ (*g*) is shaped like the back of the tongue blocking the throat, why the
vowels are built from three shapes. That chapter was lost for nearly five
hundred years, so the world had the letters but not the reasons. A surviving
copy was found in 1940. The letters worked the whole time. But a system whose
reasons are lost cannot be extended, only used.

This part is gog's reasons, published with the package on purpose. It states the
nine laws the package never breaks. It says why the engine refuses what it
refuses, and why every refusal comes with a direction. None of it is required to
*use* gog. The earlier parts cite these laws by name, and never ask you to have
read them. It is here for the moment you want to know why the grammar is shaped
the way it is. The laws also let you predict what the engine will do in a case
no chapter covers.

The laws all refuse the same thing, and it has a name: the expert's shortcut.
It saves an expert a few keystrokes and gives every beginner one more exception
to learn.
